ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC$ and $\angle B=40^\circ$. Point D moves along the line segment $BC$ (D does not coincide with B or C). Connect $AD$ and construct $\angle ADE=40^\circ$, with $DE$ intersecting line segment $AC$ at $E$. As point D moves, the shape of $\triangle ADE$ also changes. When $\triangle ADE$ is an isosceles triangle, what is the degree measure of $\angle BDA$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since AB = AC,\\
it follows that $\angle B = \angle C = 40^\circ$,\\
(1) When AD = AE, $\angle ADE = \angle AED = 40^\circ$,\\
since $\angle AED > \angle C$,\\
this case does not hold;\\
(2) When DA = DE, that is $\angle DAE = \angle DEA = \frac{1}{2}(180^\circ - 40^\circ) = 70^\circ$,\\
since $\angle BAC = 180^\circ - 40^\circ - 40^\circ = 100^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle BAD = 100^\circ - 70^\circ = 30^\circ$;\\
therefore $\angle BDA = 180^\circ - 30^\circ - 40^\circ = \boxed{110^\circ}$;\\
(3) When EA = ED, $\angle ADE = \angle DAE = 40^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle BAD = 100^\circ - 40^\circ = 60^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle BDA = 180^\circ - 60^\circ - 40^\circ = 80^\circ$;\\
therefore, when $\triangle ADE$ is an isosceles triangle, the degree of $\angle BDA$ is $110^\circ$ or $80^\circ$.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: A is the apex of triangle ABC, B and C lie on the base, D is an interior point of BC, E lies on side AC, segment AD is drawn, and the marked 40° at D is the interior angle ∠ADE. From the text AB=AC and ∠B=40°, so ∠C=40° and ∠BAC=100°. Let x=∠BDA. In triangle ABD, ∠ABD=40°, so ∠BAD=180°-40°-x=140°-x. Because AE lies along AC, ∠DAE=∠BAC-∠BAD=100°-(140°-x)=x-40°. Thus triangle ADE has angles ∠ADE=40°, ∠DAE=x-40°, and ∠AED=180°-x. For ADE to be isosceles, two of these three angles must be equal. Solve x-40=40 to get x=80°; solve x-40=180-x to get x=110°; solve 40=180-x to get x=140°, but this makes ∠BAD=0° and is degenerate, contradicting D being an interior point. Therefore the possible values are 80° and 110°.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the diagram, in $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC$ and $\angle B=40^\circ$. Point D moves along the line segment $BC$ (D does not coincide with B or C). Connect $AD$ and construct $\angle ADE=40^\circ$, with $DE$ intersecting line segment $AC$ at $E$. As point D moves, the shape of $\triangle ADE$ also changes. When $\triangle ADE$ is an isosceles triangle, what is the degree measure of $\angle BDA$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Since AB = AC,\\
it follows that $\angle B = \angle C = 40^\circ$,\\
(1) When AD = AE, $\angle ADE = \angle AED = 40^\circ$,\\
since $\angle AED > \angle C$,\\
this case does not hold;\\
(2) When DA = DE, that is $\angle DAE = \angle DEA = \frac{1}{2}(180^\circ - 40^\circ) = 70^\circ$,\\
since $\angle BAC = 180^\circ - 40^\circ - 40^\circ = 100^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle BAD = 100^\circ - 70^\circ = 30^\circ$;\\
therefore $\angle BDA = 180^\circ - 30^\circ - 40^\circ = \boxed{110^\circ}$;\\
(3) When EA = ED, $\angle ADE = \angle DAE = 40^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle BAD = 100^\circ - 40^\circ = 60^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle BDA = 180^\circ - 60^\circ - 40^\circ = 80^\circ$;\\
therefore, when $\triangle ADE$ is an isosceles triangle, the degree of $\angle BDA$ is $110^\circ$ or $80^\circ$
raw_record.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, A is a vertex of triangle ABC, B and C are on the base, D is an interior point on segment BC, and E is on side AC; AD and DE are connected in the figure, and ∠B=40° and the interior angle ∠ADE=40° at point D are marked. Then reason: Because AB=AC, △ABC is an isosceles triangle, ∠B=∠C=40°, therefore ∠BAC=180°-40°-40°=100°. Let x=∠BDA. Since D is on BC, ∠ABD=∠ABC=40°, so in △ABD, ∠BAD=180°-40°-x=140°-x. Also because AE is along the direction of AC, ∠DAE=∠BAC-∠BAD=100°-(140°-x)=x-40°. Therefore the three angles of △ADE are ∠ADE=40°, ∠DAE=x-40°, ∠AED=180°-40°-(x-40°)=180°-x. If △ADE is an isosceles triangle, then two angles are equal: first, x-40=40, giving x=80°; second, x-40=180-x, giving 2x=220, x=110°; third, 40=180-x, giving x=140°, but at this time ∠BAD=140°-140°=0°, AD coincides with AB, causing D to coincide with B, which contradicts that D does not coincide with B, so discard it. Thus the possible values of ∠BDA are 80° or 110°.
